label: encrypts keys for
type: subject = a key; object = the key or secret that the subject key encrypts. One hop of a key-wrapping hierarchy.
note: Filed once and used by TWO key hierarchies that round 26 deliberately did not merge: native encryption at rest (encryption-at-rest key -> DEK -> data) and system secrets (master key -> data key -> on-disk secrets). That the same predicate fits both is evidence they are the same KIND of construction, and is not evidence they are the same keys - the things protected differ and no page relates them. Recording the shared predicate while keeping the concept hierarchies separate is the honest position, and it is what lets a future SME answer the question in one place instead of re-deriving it.
relates_to_competency_question: What encrypts a given key, and what does that key encrypt in turn?
